subject: Re: Dedicated capacity briefing for Clearview Analytics — scheduling
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@clearview.ai>
To: support@redwood.inference <support@redwood.inference>, ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity interest — Clearview Analytics

Hi Ben / Redwood team,

I signed up through the self-serve flow yesterday (account: clearview.redwood) and we're evaluating Dedicated capacity for a production rollout of our document-processing pipeline. Quick context: we expect bursty traffic up to ~450 concurrent requests during business hours, average 600 tokens per request, and a 99th-percentile tail latency target of ~300ms for the user-facing endpoints.

I've attached a small sample of our request distribution and some synthetic load numbers — please see "clearview-load-profile.csv". We'd like a short walkthrough focused on sizing (throughput/latency tradeoffs) and any recommended quantization/kv-cache settings for our workload.

Would someone be able to run an initial capacity briefing this week? Prefer afternoons PT. Also, are you able to run a quick smoke test if we provide a small S3 dataset?

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Head of Platform
Clearview Analytics
[Attachment: clearview-load-profile.csv (csv)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@clearview.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity interest — Clearview Analytics

Hi Sarah — great to meet you and thanks for the context. I'm Ben (SDR, Redwood Inference) and I'll coordinate a short technical briefing with our Capacity team.

Quick asks so we make the call focused and useful:
- Which model(s) are you planning to serve (open-source / fine-tuned)?
- Is the 450 concurrent requests figure peak instantaneous concurrency or sustained within a 1-minute window?
- Do you have a preferred SLO for p50/p95/p99 latencies beyond the p99 target you mentioned?

I can ringfence a 30-minute slot for a briefing and pull in an engineer for sizing. Here are three PT slots that work on our side:
- Tue 2026-04-13 13:00 PT
- Tue 2026-04-13 15:30 PT
- Wed 2026-04-14 14:00 PT

Pick one and I'll send a calendar invite. Also happy to accept a calendar invite from your side.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/CV-2026-1987
Calendar (if easier): https://cal.example.com/booking/ben_carter/30min

We can also run a short smoke test; if you want that, please send an S3 temporary URL and sample input format and we can queue a run during the call.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Development Representative
Redwood Inference

Things I'll pull together before the call:
- A quick run-book of tests we'll perform during the briefing
- Suggested canary/fallback policies for spike handling
- A short slide with estimated cost vs latency at 95/99 percentiles

If Laura's ok, I'll include the "RID_capacity_estimate_Clearview_20260413.xlsx" as a draft in the invite; Ben, hold the 13:00 PT slot as tentative until Sarah picks.

Thanks,
Hannah

Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@clearview.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@clearview.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity interest — Clearview Analytics

Hi Ben — thanks, 13:00 PT on Tue works for us. Confirming some more detail before the call:
- Model: open-source Llama 2 13B (fp16, not currently quantized)
- 450 concurrent is peak instantaneous during batch ingest windows (roughly 09:00–11:30 PT), otherwise 60–80 concurrent off-peak
- Target: p50 ~ 50–80ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 300ms

I've attached a short packet with traffic slices and a sample request payload. We're happy for you to run a smoke test on the sample dataset during the call — I'll put an S3 presigned URL in a follow-up if that's okay.

Also, one ask: can the briefing cover autoscale policy recommendations and whether Reserved (Dedicated) capacity with burst pools makes sense vs. pure on-demand?

Thanks,
Sarah
[Attachment: clearview-qps-summary.pdf (pdf)]
